title: Country names and query language shifted AI answers in different ways
summary: In tests with three language models, naming a country in the user’s message moved open-ended responses 30–44% closer to the same model’s answers when assigned that country as a persona. Changing the query language instead shifted multiple-choice responses away from the associated persona in all three models.
organization: University of Copenhagen; Aalborg University Copenhagen; Bocconi University

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 §§3–5.2, Figure 2, annotation and translation sensitivity appendices

evidence.tested: The controlled study compared named-country and language cues across survey-derived choices and about 1.6 million open-ended responses.
evidence.unknown: The reference was each model’s own persona-conditioned responses rather than people’s values. Country and language stand in for only a small part of cultural identity, and the measured shifts depended on prompt design.
evidence.ai_role: Llama, Ministral and Gemma generate answers under matched national persona, named-country and language cues; learned annotation and translation models support value comparisons.
